variants.headline: Party divides in two
variants.sub: The colony has seen a party divide into two organisations.
variants.body:
A political party has split in two in {colony}. The division is an organisational fact, not a complete explanation of the differences behind it. In considering {target}, readers should distinguish the break itself from unreported motives, ideological labels or claims about the balance of parliamentary strength.

An organisational division in politics is not the same as a change in the rules under which firms operate. Commercial readers should avoid treating the split as a ready-made forecast. Representation and future decisions require examination in their own right, without an assumed programme attached to either part.

We support {target} in this assessment. Unity is not an unlimited obligation, and a fair political judgment must allow that separation can deserve defence rather than automatic condemnation for breaking ranks. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
